title: Over-the-air RF transmission check of LTM-1C stack with tinySA spectrum analyzer and handheld radio
summary: A stacked PCB assembly labelled "LTM-1C" sits next to a tinySA spectrum analyzer that has a telescopic whip antenna on its HIGH input, sweeping about 240–959 MHz. A handheld transceiver with a stubby SMA antenna is in the foreground. For the first ~2.5 s the marker tracks ambient peaks near 502 MHz at about -51 to -52 dBm. At ~2.8 s a green LED lights on the LTM-1C and the handheld's display backlight comes on. By ~3.8 s the marker jumps to a new sharp peak at 436.5 MHz (about -40 to -47 dBm). The peak stays until ~7.3 s, then the LED goes off and the handheld backlight turns off at ~7.85 s.
test_objective: Check that an RF transmission near 436.5 MHz (70 cm UHF band, maybe a downlink from the LTM-1C payload or a keyed handheld) can be seen with the tinySA. It should appear as a clear peak above the ambient noise floor while the transmit indicator is on, and go away or drop when transmission stops.

equipment.name: LTM-1C stacked PCB assembly (green board with FPGA/MCU, purple boards below, status LED)
tinySA spectrum analyzer (SEESII), HIGH input, START 240 MHz, STOP ~959 MHz, 71.9 MHz/div
Telescopic whip antenna on tinySA HIGH SMA port
Handheld UHF/VHF transceiver with stubby SMA antenna (blue backlit LCD)
USB cables (mini-USB to LTM-1C, braided USB-C to tinySA)

steps.action: Operator watches the tinySA sweep with no transmission active (LTM-1C LED off, handheld display dark).
steps.observation: Baseline spectrum. Marker auto-tracks the highest ambient peak near 501.9–502.4 MHz at about -50.4 to -52.4 dBm. No distinct peak at 436 MHz.

steps.action: Transmission starts: the LTM-1C green LED lights and the handheld display backlight comes on (radio keyed or receiving).
steps.observation: Marker still reads 502.1 MHz at -51.4 dBm, so the sweep has not caught the new signal yet.

steps.action: Transmission continues; operator watches the analyzer.
steps.observation: New sharp peak at 436.5 MHz becomes the strongest signal: -40.4 dBm, then -46.9 dBm, -47.4 dBm, and about -42 dBm. LED stays green.

steps.action: Transmission ends (handheld backlight off; LED still on).
steps.observation: Marker at 436.3 MHz, level down to -50.4 dBm, so the signal is fading.

test_case.title: Over-the-air detection of the 436.5 MHz UHF transmission from the LTM-1C setup
test_case.objective: Check that a transmission near 436.5 MHz shows up on a spectrum analyzer as a distinct peak clearly above the ambient level, and that it matches the transmit indicator.
preconditions: LTM-1C stack is powered over USB and running transmit-capable firmware
tinySA is charged or USB-powered, with a valid self-test/calibration
Handheld radio is charged and set to about 436.5 MHz
Operating on 436.5 MHz is permitted (licence or shielded environment)
setup: Fit the telescopic whip antenna to the tinySA HIGH input (+10 dBm max input)
Set the tinySA to HIGH mode, START 240 MHz, STOP ~959 MHz, auto RBW, marker 1 on peak tracking
Place the LTM-1C, the handheld and the tinySA antenna within about 0.5 m of each other on a non-metallic bench

procedure.action: With no transmission active, record the tinySA marker frequency and level for about 2 s.
procedure.expected_result: Baseline peak is ambient (here ~502 MHz, about -52 dBm). No distinct carrier at 436.5 MHz.

procedure.action: Start the transmission (trigger the LTM-1C TX or key the handheld).
procedure.expected_result: The LTM-1C green status LED and/or handheld indicator turns on.
Marker moves to about 436.5 MHz ±0.2 MHz, with a level at least 5 dB above the baseline peak (about -40 to -47 dBm seen).

procedure.action: Hold the transmission for about 4 s and record the marker readings.
procedure.expected_result: Peak stays at about 436.5 MHz with a stable level and no large spurious products.
Indicator turns off; the 436.5 MHz peak drops back to ambient level within 1–2 sweeps.

pass_criteria: Carrier is detected at 436.5 MHz ±0.2 MHz only while transmitting
Peak level is at least 5 dB above the ambient baseline
Signal disappears or drops after transmission stops
fail_criteria: No peak near 436.5 MHz while transmitting
Carrier is off-frequency by more than 0.2 MHz
Carrier stays after TX stops, or strong spurious emissions appear
LED/indicator state does not match the RF activity
teardown: Turn off the handheld and the tinySA
Unplug USB power from the LTM-1C
Collapse the whip antenna and store the equipment

assumptions: It's unclear whether the 436.5 MHz signal comes from the LTM-1C or the handheld radio. Both indicators turn on at about the same time.
The frequency band and purpose (e.g. a satellite payload UHF downlink) are inferred from the 436.5 MHz reading and the board label.
The stop frequency (~959 MHz) is only partly legible.
Frequency tolerance and the level margin in the pass criteria are proposed by me; the video doesn't show them.
No operator hand actions are visible. The transmission was presumably triggered off-camera.
